text:
SoftBank alone has taken $7.4 billion out of India through exits like Flipkart, Paytm and Policybazaar. Japan's money in Indian startups goes far beyond one big fund.

Japanese investors now write cheques at every stage here, from deep-tech seed funds in Bengaluru to bank-backed funds and corporate VCs like Sony's. Razorpay, Meesho and Lenskart all have Japanese backers.

In this carousel: 8 Japanese investors that back Indian founders, with their stage, cheque size, Indian portfolio and how to reach each one.

Quick tip: Japanese investors usually take longer to decide and value long-term relationships. Start the conversation early, share regular updates before you ask for money, and show why Japan matters for your business if you want strategic help, not just capital.

text:
Y Combinator lists 177 companies headquartered in India, including Razorpay, Meesho, Groww and Zepto. US money has been backing Indian founders from day zero for over a decade.

And it is not only YC. US grant programmes, founder fellowships and seed funds now run India cohorts, and big US VCs have Bengaluru teams writing seed cheques.

In this carousel: 8 US investors that back Indian founders, with their deal terms, stage, Indian portfolio and how to apply.

Quick tip: check the entity rule before you apply. YC and many US funds can only invest in a US or similar parent company, so a "flip" may be needed. Talk to a lawyer early and ask about the tax cost. Grants like Emergent Ventures need no flip at all.
